title: Chow module with finite cohomology and generic rank one
statement: Let $f:X\to T$ be proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], with $T$ affine and $R=\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$ Noetherian, and $i:W\to X$ a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] with $W$ integral [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Put $\eta=\operatorname{genericPoint}(W)$ and $\xi=i(\eta)$. There exists a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $G$ [pqf-def-coherent] whose support, the nonzero-stalk locus [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], is $i(W)$, whose stalk $G_\xi$ is annihilated by $\mathfrak m_\xi$, and which admits a $\kappa(\xi)$-module structure [def-weil-residue-field] compatible with the original $\mathcal O_{X,\xi}$ action through the residue map and with dimension one. For every $q\ge0$, $H^q(X,G)$ [pqf-def-cohomology] is a finite $R$-module for the scalar action restricted along $f.\mathrm{appTop}$.

proof.text: The affine Noetherian base is Noetherian. Apply ChowModification to g=i followed by f, using its properness instances. Set Y, pi, N and j to the existing Chow construction, and construct L explicitly as the usual double pullback of the integral O(1). Obtain n, coherence and finite cohomology for G=i_* pi_* L^n from the specified-twist theorem.

The integral polynomial Proj twist is invertible; pullback and tensor powers preserve invertibility. Chow supplies U dense with pi restricted to U an isomorphism. Apply the birational-line stalk comparison to L^n to obtain e:G_xi additive-equivalent to kappa(xi), respecting quotient scalars.

Coherence on the locally Noetherian X gives quasi-coherence and finite type, hence closed support. Closed pushforward gives zero stalks off i(W). The additive equivalence to the nontrivial residue field puts xi in the support. For every w in W, the generic point specializes to w; continuity of i and stability of closed sets under specialization put i(w) in the support. Thus the support equals i(W).

Residue(a)=0 for a in the maximal ideal; the scalar compatibility of e and injectivity give a v=0. Transfer the residue-field module structure through the additive equivalence e, retaining the existing additive group. The transported e is a linear equivalence, so compatibility and finrank_self give the desired scalar identity and dimension one. Combine these with the already obtained coherence, support equality and finite cohomology.

proof_origin.note: Q2 formalized the assembly from the specified-twist finiteness and birational-line stalk comparison; the topological support and algebraic residue-module arguments are proved in Lean.
